newsitem.title: USA: BPA lowers Monday power prices, limits peak sales.
newsitem.headline: BPA lowers Monday power prices, limits peak sales.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) slightly lowered prices for surplus power sales on Monday, but continued to hold off from offering power during morning or evening peaks, the agency said Friday.

BPA offered non-firm power during hours ending 1200-1800 PDT and 2200 PDT on Monday at $13.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) for Northwest deliveries and $14.00 for Califoria-Oregon border (COB), down $2.00 from Friday prices.
Prices for non-firm power for hours ending at 0600 PDT and 2300 PDT were 50 cents lower at $9.50 for all deliveries.
Prices for off-peak non-firm power during hours ending 0100-0500 PDT and 2400 PDT were also cut by 50 cents to $9.00.
Firm power during off-peak hours on Monday was also 50 cents lower at $9.00.
